newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends weak due to holidays.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends weak due to holidays.

text.p: The Singapore rubber trade closed softly on Monday as a string of holidays, weak sentiment and the unresolved strike at Goodyear Tire hung like a millstone over the market, dealers said.
The Golden Week holidays in Japan running until May 5, the May day holiday on Thursday, and an industry dinner in the Thai rubber centre of Hat Yai on Friday will keep most in the trade sidelined.
"All those holidays will discourage any aggressive moves by people in the trade. The Goodyear strike is bad for the market the longer it lasts," a dealer said.
Traders said volume in the market remained thin.
"Most of the buyers were out. There's very little action going on," one dealer said, adding the Goodyear strike may slowly push down prices of SIR20 rubber in Indonesia.
Traders said SIR20 rubber was seen at around 46.00-46.50 U.S. cents a lb in Palembang. "It should drift slowly down to 45 cents," a dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 107.50 U.S. cents a kg from 107.00 cents. July RSS1 was seen at 156.00-158.00 Singapore cents (US$1.08-$1.09) a kg from 155.75 cents.
